1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/disposition.sh — the disposition vocabulary and the engine's
3	# response table (issue #1822, ADR-054 §6).
4	#
5	# ONE question — "is this failure recoverable?" — answered ONCE, here, from a
6	# field the stage declared. Before this file, four stages answered it four ways:
7	# build's `did_not_finish` carve-out (#1208), design's separate copy of it
8	# (#1261), plan's hand-rolled `return 1` that killed the whole run, and test's
9	# nothing-at-all (#1747). Every new stage added a fifth answer.
10	#
11	# `disposition` is a CLOSED set owned by the engine. #2187 (ADR-054 §6 amended):
12	# each word names a CAUSE a reader must be able to tell apart; many words share
13	# one ACTION. The word never carries a retry count — the template's per-stage
14	# `retry:` budget does:
15	#
16	#   complete       the stage ran; its verdict says how it went      → proceed
17	#   unusable       it ran, but its output cannot be used           → retry
18	#   timed_out      it ran out of time                              → retry
19	#   out_of_turns   it ran out of turn budget                       → retry
20	#   interrupted    an outside signal stopped it                    → retry
21	#   throttled      a short rate limit, recovering                  → wait, retry
22	#   rate_limited   the account's usage limit                       → end run, resumable
23	#   unavailable    an external service zBuild depends on is not    → end run, resumable
24	#                  responding (model provider, GitHub, git remote)
25	#   misconfigured  the setup is wrong (operator fixes it)          → halt
26	#   broken         a defect in zBuild (file a bug)                 → halt
27	#
28	#   (`exhausted` was retired by #2187: it mapped to `escalate`, which nothing
29	#   implemented, and it hid WHICH budget ran out — timed_out / out_of_turns say.)
30	#
31	# The response table lives HERE, not in any plugin: no stage decides its own
32	# retry policy. A stage declares what happened; the engine decides what to do.
33	#
34	# Two rules the rest of the engine depends on:
35	#   - A disposition outside the set is a STRUCTURAL FAILURE. No default is ever
36	#     invented. Inventing one is how "unrecognized is never a failure" — the
37	#     #1819 generator defect — grows back.
38	#   - `broken` is the engine's OWN conclusion about a dispatch that explained
39	#     nothing. The engine never writes it into the stage's artifact; it holds it
40	#     on its own channels (`runner_read_stage_disposition`, the dispatch event).
41	#
42	# NOT in this file, deliberately: the re-dispatch mechanism. ADR-054's delivery
43	# map gives #1822 the vocabulary and the table; nothing owns the loop yet, and
44	# no plugin emits a v2 result to drive one (`grep result_contract plugins/` is
45	# empty). `disposition_retryable` / `disposition_wait_s` state the policy so the
46	# loop, when it lands, reads it instead of re-deriving it.
47	#
48	# Name collision, for the record: ADR-021's member-disposition contract already
49	# writes `.disposition` on plugin primaries with an unrelated vocabulary
50	# (terminal|recoverable|advisory|none — see `_cycle_member_terminal_failure` in
51	# cycle-orchestrator.sh). The two axes are genuinely different: ADR-021 asks
52	# "this stage's verdict was fail — does that stop the cycle?", ADR-054 asks "did
53	# the stage get far enough to produce a verdict worth reading?". They chain; they
54	# do not overlap. #2161: the collision stopped being inert when the acceptance
55	# gate declared `result_contract: 2` — its first fully green run was refused by
56	# this reader. The ADR-021 word now lives in `severity`; `disposition` is this
57	# set only. Readers of the policy word fall back to `disposition` for v1-shaped
58	# results.
59	
60	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_SH_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
61	_ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_SH_LOADED=1
62	
63	# The closed set, in ADR-054 §6 table order.
64	_ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_SET="complete unusable timed_out out_of_turns interrupted throttled rate_limited unavailable misconfigured broken"
65	
66	# How long a `throttled` stage waits before a retry. Overridable because the

71	# ─── disposition_vocabulary ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
72	# The closed set, space-separated, in table order. Callers iterate this rather
73	# than restating the words — a second copy of the list is a second contract.
74	disposition_vocabulary() {
75	    printf '%s' "$_ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_SET"
76	}
77	
78	# ─── disposition_is_valid <disposition> ─────────────────────────────────────
79	# rc 0 when the word is a member of the closed set, 1 otherwise. An empty
80	# string is NOT a member: a v1 result declares no disposition at all, and that
81	# absence is distinct from any of the six words.
82	disposition_is_valid() {
83	    local d="${1-}"
84	    [[ -n "$d" ]] || return 1
85	    case " $_ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_SET " in
86	        *" $d "*) return 0 ;;
87	        *)        return 1 ;;
88	    esac
89	}
90	
91	# ─── disposition_response <disposition> ─────────────────────────────────────
92	# THE response table. Prints the engine's response and returns 0 for a member of
93	# the set; prints nothing and returns 1 for anything else.
94	#
95	# Refusing to answer for an unknown word is the point: a caller that wants a
96	# response for `wedged` has already failed structurally, and handing it back a
97	# plausible-looking default would bury that.
98	#
99	# `unavailable` and `broken` both stop the run but are NOT interchangeable — an
100	# operator reading the log has to distinguish "something outside us is down, a
101	# human needs to act" from "this is our own defect". They differ in what is
102	# reported, not in the stopping.
103	disposition_response() {
104	    case "${1-}" in
105	        complete)                         printf 'proceed' ;;
106	        unusable|timed_out|out_of_turns)  printf 'retry' ;;
107	        interrupted)                      printf 'retry' ;;
108	        throttled)                        printf 'retry_after_wait' ;;
109	        rate_limited|unavailable)         printf 'halt_unavailable' ;;
110	        misconfigured)                    printf 'halt_misconfigured' ;;
111	        broken)                           printf 'halt_broken' ;;
112	        *)                                return 1 ;;
113	    esac
114	}
115	
116	# ─── disposition_halts <disposition> ────────────────────────────────────────
117	# rc 0 when the engine must stop the run. Derived from the response table rather
118	# than restating it, so the two can never disagree.
119	# A non-member HALTS (#1850, ADR-054 §4 — it was a third rc, 2): an unknown word
120	# is a structural failure, so the one safe answer is to stop.
121	disposition_halts() {
122	    local r; r="$(disposition_response "${1-}")" || return 0
123	    case "$r" in
124	        halt_*) return 0 ;;
125	        *)      return 1 ;;
126	    esac
127	}
128	
129	# ─── disposition_retryable <disposition> ────────────────────────────────────
130	# rc 0 when the engine may re-dispatch the stage. Retry is a property of the
131	# DISPOSITION, not of the stage — this is the inversion ADR-054 §6 describes.
132	# Derived from the response table, which is what makes "nothing both halts and
133	# retries" structurally true rather than a rule someone has to remember.
134	# A non-member is not retryable: it halts (see disposition_halts), and nothing
135	# both halts and retries.
136	disposition_retryable() {
137	    local r; r="$(disposition_response "${1-}")" || return 1
138	    case "$r" in
139	        retry|retry_after_wait) return 0 ;;
140	        *)                      return 1 ;;
141	    esac
142	}
143	
144	# ─── disposition_unfinished <disposition> (#2187) ──────────────────────────
145	# rc 0 when the word says the stage stopped before finishing its work — out of
146	# time, out of turns, or stopped by an outside signal. The cycle reads this, not
147	# a specific word, when it asks "did this iteration finish?".
148	disposition_unfinished() {
149	    case "${1-}" in
150	        timed_out|out_of_turns|interrupted) return 0 ;;
151	        *)                                  return 1 ;;
152	    esac
153	}
154	
155	# ─── disposition_wait_s <disposition> ───────────────────────────────────────
156	# Seconds to wait before re-dispatching. What separates `interrupted` from
157	# `throttled` is not the word but this number: a throttled stage re-dispatched
158	# immediately is simply throttled again, which is a retry loop that burns budget
159	# to learn nothing. Non-members return 1 and print nothing.
160	disposition_wait_s() {
161	    local d="${1-}"
162	    disposition_is_valid "$d" || return 1
163	    # A wait is meaningless for a disposition that is not going to be retried,
164	    # and answering "0" for one is actively dangerous: a caller that skipped
165	    # `disposition_retryable` would read "0 seconds until retry" for `broken`
166	    # and re-dispatch a halted stage immediately. Refuse instead of returning a
167	    # plausible-looking number.
168	    disposition_retryable "$d" || return 1
169	    if [[ "$d" != "throttled" ]]; then
170	        printf '0'
171	        return 0
172	    fi
173	    local w="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_THROTTLE_WAIT_S:-$_ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_THROTTLE_WAIT_DEFAULT}"
174	    # Environment input: must be a positive integer within a sane bound, else
175	    # fall back to the default rather than honouring a value that would hang a
176	    # run or defeat the wait entirely.
177	    if [[ "$w" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$w" -ge 1 ]] && [[ "$w" -le 3600 ]]; then
178	        printf '%s' "$w"
179	    else
180	        printf '%s' "$_ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_THROTTLE_WAIT_DEFAULT"
181	    fi
182	}

9	## Context
10	
11	Three consecutive discoveries of the same abort-propagation bug class —
12	each at a different dispatch site — have shipped tactical per-site fixes
13	that did not generalize:
14	
15	1. **#612 (Wave 8)** — `route_to_model_loop` did not distinguish a
16	   SIGINT-driven child exit (rc=130) from a generic per-iteration failure

21	   The trap installer (`_route_loop_install_traps`) and signal

23	2. **#616 (Wave 8)** — same bug class one layer up: the build plugin
24	   captured rc=130 from the router but then ran post-processing as if the
25	   call had succeeded, returning rc=0 to the runner. Tactical fix added an

32	   Wave 8 shipped, so it never received the per-site SIGINT pattern) has
33	   the third instance of the same gap. `_cycle_iter_dispatch` at
34	   `core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:664-681` captures `rc=$?` from
35	   `cycle_dispatch_stage`, increments `fail` if non-zero, and continues to

39	The pattern is now clear: every new dispatcher recreates the bug. Per-site

41	issue, not the class. The cycle orchestrator gap is the third instance;
42	the next dispatcher (strategy plugins, future orchestrators) is one
43	unchecked `rc=$?` away from re-discovery.

46	authors how to propagate abort across nested dispatch layers, plus a
47	cross-subshell signal channel for cases where rc propagation alone is too
48	slow (a child that hasn't returned yet when a sibling child sees the
49	abort).

70	This means the SIGTERM widening in #686 is a one-line change to the
71	helper's classifier (add 143 to the recognised set) and does not change
72	the helper's signature or the call-site contract. Every dispatcher calls
73	it immediately after capturing each child rc. Greppable —
74	`grep -r _zbuild_propagate_abort` enumerates every dispatch site
75	participating in the contract. Single point to evolve when SIGTERM parity
76	ships.

1	# ADR-054: Stage Contract
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (2026-08-09)
4	**Date:** 2026-08-09
5	**Issue:** #1820
6	**Amended:** 2026-10-07 (#1798) — §4: a leaf stage whose verdict is fail-class ends the run unless its template marks it `blocking: false` (Amendment at the end).
7	**Amended:** 2026-09-16 (#2111) — §6: a rate limit observed by the router resolves to `unavailable`, not `throttled`. The engine now enforces `halt_unavailable` on the cycle dispatch path (it was announced only): the run ends `aborted` with `reason=llm_rate_limited` and the reset text under `.rate_limit.message`, state persisted for ADR-050 resume. `throttled` stays in the closed set with no rate-limit emitter. Waiting and retrying re-entered the same limit for five iterations on #1840/#1841, re-verifying an unchanged tree each time.
8	**Amended:** 2026-08-23 (#141) — §7: the three-actor table is run-keyed in every row; the **issue** is a second scope, and `release` gains the `always-run` attribute plus a `persist` sibling (ADR-059).
9	**Amended:** 2026-08-23 (#1920) — §7: the `release` "deletes nothing" promise scoped to the run's own lifecycle; operator-invoked reclamation (`zbuild cleanup --state-dirs`) named as a third actor with its own clock and guards.
10	**Amended:** 2026-08-12 (#1862) — §3.1 added: the engine exports dispatch identity (`ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE`, `ZBUILD_PLUGIN`, `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND`, `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR`) at `plugin_hook_call`, scoped to one dispatch. A plugin is self-defining about what it is and can never be self-defining about which stage it serves. `ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT` is explicitly excluded; identity is scrubbed by `env-scrub` per ADR-024, not exempted from it.
11	**Amends:**
12	- ADR-001 — the stage contract is two hooks (§1), rc ∈ {0,1} (§4), and one result file (§5). The rc=1→`kind: recovery` routing is deleted; it was never implemented and no recovery plugin was ever registered.
13	- ADR-021 — verdict and disposition are separated (§6); the informally-inherited `pass|warn|fail|unknown|error|corrupt_diff|block` set, which carried both axes in one string, is replaced.
14	- ADR-025 — the runner still owns the trap, but `cleanup` is no longer an abort-only notification: it is dispatched by a `teardown` stage with a `scope` (§7).
15	- ADR-045 — superseded by the same verdict/disposition split (§6).
16	**Related:** ADR-001 (plugin contract), ADR-013 (canonical stage list), ADR-017 (per-stage router config), ADR-047 (stage-agnostic mechanics — the parent principle this extends), ADR-055 (inter-stage data contract v2), ADR-056 (run+cleanup-only lifecycle)
17	
18	## Context
19	
20	**This ADR is a specification, not a description.** It states the contract Phase 0 (#1819) implements; each section names the issue that delivers it. Where the engine does not yet behave this way, that is recorded as the gap it is — the whole reason for writing it down.
21	
22	ADR-001 defined the general plugin contract for all plugin kinds. The stage-bound subset was never extracted, and the parts of ADR-001 that touched it were aspirational in a way nothing ever reconciled:
23	
24	| ADR-001 said | The engine did |
25	|---|---|
26	| Four hooks: `init`, `run`, `finalize`, `cleanup` | Five `plugin_hook_call` sites, **all `run`**. Three of the four were never called — including `cleanup`, which 20+ plugins nevertheless implement. |
27	| `rc=1` routes to `kind: recovery` plugins; `rc=2` is fatal | **No recovery plugin has ever been registered.** Stages return 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 143. |
28	| `valid_verdicts` declares a plugin's vocabulary | ~~**No engine code reads it.** Adoption: 1 of 25.~~ **Closed by #1708**: adoption is 25 of 25, and `scripts/lib/lint-verdict-classify.sh` fails the build when a declared verdict is not classified. |
29	
30	The pattern is one defect, not three: **a declaration nothing enforces.** An unknown verdict draws a yellow glyph; an undeclared hook returns `0` silently; a zero-byte artifact passes the fail-closed scanner. Unrecognized is never a failure, so the document and the engine were free to drift apart for the life of the project.
31	
32	ADR-054 fixes the call and response surfaces — hooks, arguments, exit codes, the result file, and the verdict/disposition split. ADR-055 fixes the data and declaration surfaces. Together they are the interface Phase 0 enforces.
33	
34	### Why this precedes the rest of Initiative 1.3
35	
36	Initiative 1.3 (#1818) is one defect wearing different clothes across seven phases: the engine and its stages have no enforced interface. Phase 1 (#1794) makes a failing leaf stage stop the run — the single most valuable change in the milestone, and **unshippable without this contract**.
37	
38	Today a router timeout surfaces as `verdict=error`. Make a failing verdict terminal without first separating *what happened* from *what to do about it*, and a network hiccup on `intake` or `impact` becomes a dead run. `interrupted` and `throttled` exist so that the same event can stop a run that is genuinely broken and retry one that merely stalled. That is the whole reason the disposition vocabulary (§6) is a declared field rather than a string the engine re-interprets.
39	
40	The same dependency runs through the rest: Phase 3 cannot enforce declarations that were never load-bearing (ADR-055), Phase 4 cannot safely delete code whose reachability nothing can prove, and Phase 5's acceptance work measures assertions against a result file whose shape this ADR fixes. **Every phase either depends on this contract or is a consequence of not having had one.**
41	
42	## Decision
43	
44	### 1. The call surface: two hooks
45	
46	The contract has exactly **two** hooks:
47	
48	| Hook | Required | Invoked by |
49	|------|----------|------------|
50	| `run` | Yes | Every stage dispatch |
51	| `cleanup` | No | A `teardown` stage, with a `scope` (§7) |
52	
53	`init` and `finalize` are deleted from the contract. ADR-056 (#1828) carries out that deletion and owns the resulting lifecycle — including registration-time enforcement of `run` and the `rc=3` sentinel that distinguishes an absent optional hook from one that ran. This ADR does not restate those rules; it specifies the two surviving hooks' arguments (§2) and `cleanup`'s trigger and scope (§7).
54	
55	**What was true before this contract.** Three of the four hooks ADR-001 documented were never called: there are five `plugin_hook_call` sites in the engine and every one passes `run`. `init` and `finalize` were dead. `cleanup` was also dead — never dispatched by anything — yet **20+ plugins ship one**, written to a documented interface and drifting untested for the life of the project. That is the failure mode this ADR exists to end: a document describing a lifecycle the engine implemented one fifth of, with nothing reconciling the two.
56	
57	### 2. Hook signatures
58	
59	```
60	run(stage_id, state_file, resolved_inputs)
61	cleanup(stage_id, state_file, scope)
62	```
63	
64	- `stage_id` — the dispatching stage's id.
65	- `state_file` — absolute path to `pipeline-state.json`. Plugins derive `state_dir = dirname($2)` and `artifacts_dir = $state_dir/artifacts`.
66	- `resolved_inputs` — the engine resolves every input the manifest declares and hands them over. **A plugin never rebuilds a path.** Delivered by #1826; until then a plugin reads its declared inputs itself.
67	- `scope` — `release` or `purge` (§7).
68	
69	### 3. Runtime environment
70	
71	Run-time context is passed via env vars exported by the runner — never via positional args. The current set for stage-bound hooks:
72	
73	| Env var | Set by | Available to |
74	|---------|--------|--------------|
75	| `ZBUILD_GOAL` | runner | all hooks |
76	| `ZBUILD_ISSUE` | runner | all hooks (empty string when absent) |
77	| `ZBUILD_RUN_ID` | runner | all hooks |
78	| `ZBUILD_TARGET_PLATFORM` | runner (fanout strategy) | role-resolved hooks only |
79	| `ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE` | `plugin_hook_call` (§3.1) | all stage-bound hooks |
80	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN` | `plugin_hook_call` (§3.1) | all stage-bound hooks |
81	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND` | `plugin_hook_call` (§3.1) | all stage-bound hooks |
82	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR` | `plugin_hook_call` (§3.1) | all stage-bound hooks |
83	
84	`ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE` (PR #438) is the key the per-stage router knob resolver uses to look up `router.timeout_s`, `router.max_turns`, `router.max_iterations`, `router.retries`, and `router.tier` (ADR-017).
85	
86	#### 3.1 Dispatch identity — amended 2026-08-12 (#1862)
87	
88	**The engine states, for exactly the span of one dispatch, which stage this is and which plugin serves it.** The single export point is `plugin_hook_call` (`core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh`).
89	
90	| Variable | Value | Source |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| `ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE` | the dispatching stage's name | `stage_id` — `$1` of the hook signature (§2) |
93	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN` | the serving plugin's `id` | `$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml` |
94	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND` | the serving plugin's `kind` | `$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml` |
95	| `ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR` | the serving plugin's directory | `$1` of `plugin_hook_call` |
96	| `ZBUILD_UNIT` | this unit's own name: the stage, or `<stage>.<element>` for a map member — `<stage>.<role>.<element>` when the map runs more than one role (amended 2026-10-03, #1706) | `stage_id` plus the element the map generator bakes into the work unit |
97	
98	**Why the engine and not the plugin.** A plugin is self-defining about *what it is* — `scripts/lib/plugin-bootstrap.sh` resolves `_ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR` from the plugin's own `BASH_SOURCE`, needing no engine. It can never be self-defining about *which stage it is currently serving*. Stage name, role and plugin id are three distinct namespaces and only the template holds the mapping: `review_lenses` (stage) is served by `review-lens` (plugin id) via role `review_lens`, and under `map:` all six lens members receive that one stage name. Everything keyed to the flow — the run timeline, `stage_statuses`, the per-stage router knobs — needs the stage name; introspection yields only the plugin id.
99	
100	The engine's answer cannot differ from the plugin's own: `plugin_hook_call` sources `plugin.sh` from the same directory it stamps, and reads `id`/`kind` from the same manifest the plugin would. It is the plugin's answer plus the axis the plugin cannot reach.

3	# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
4	# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
5	# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.
6

8	_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1

10	# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}

52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
53	# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
54	# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
55	#
56	# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
57	# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
58	# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
59	# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
60	# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
61	_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
62	    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
63	    # as an option.
64	    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
65	    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
66	    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
67	    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
68	        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
69	        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
71	    done
72	    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
73	}

77	# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
78	_zbuild_pg_grace() {
79	    local _g="${1:-1}"
80	    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
81	}

87	# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
88	# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
89	# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
90	# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
91	# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.

6	# llm_unavailable | llm_rate_limited | scope_too_large — in the process
7	# (`_ZB_ABORT_REASON`) and in the sentinel file ${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal

9	# no rc carries the reason any more (it used to: 130, 143, 6, 9, 10).
10	#
11	#   A1 _zbuild_abort <word> records it, in-process and in the sentinel; returns 1
12	#   A2 the first recorded abort wins — a later one does not overwrite it
13	#   A3 _zbuild_abort_reason reads it back, from the sentinel when the process
14	#      has none (a sibling subshell recorded it)
15	#   A4 _zbuild_propagate_abort <rc> → 1 only when rc≠0 AND an abort is recorded
16	#   A5 _zbuild_check_abort → 1 when an abort is recorded, else 0
17	#   A6 arm/disarm: arming writes the word (default sigint); disarming clears
18	#      both channels

1	# ADR-065 — Process budget: the engine's fork count is a tested contract
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted (2026-09-19)
4	**Issue:** #2151
5	**Related:** ADR-001 (Discovery + lockfile), ADR-012 (test tiering), ADR-053 (test flake policy — the serial-pin cap that also needs an amendment to raise), ADR-041 (the fd-9 lock discipline the trace harness must respect)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	zBuild is bash. Every `$(jq …)`, `$(dirname …)`, `$(awk …)` is a fork and an exec, and the
10	engine does them by the thousand: on 2026-09-19 `source core/pipeline/runner.sh` execs 1,375
11	processes before any stage runs (1,050 of them `awk`), and a mocked seven-stage pipeline run
12	(`tests/golden/parity/run-fixture.sh`) execs about 7,100. The suite is therefore fork-bound, not
13	compute-bound: #1840 run 1 (35184719395) spent 4,910 of its 6,989 CPU-seconds in the kernel
14	creating processes. Fork throughput scales with cores, so the same suite takes ~15 minutes on a
15	10-core Mac and ~58 minutes inside the daemon's `test` stage on a 4-vCPU GitHub runner — the
16	single largest cost in every long run. Buying larger runners was considered and rejected: it
17	hides the cost rather than removing it.
18	
19	A census by call site (bash xtrace with `PS4='+@${BASH_SOURCE[0]-}:${LINENO}@ '`) put a third
20	of the mocked run's execs on one line — `core/pipeline/input-resolve.sh:113`, an awk per manifest
21	inside `_inputs_scan_manifests`, whose memo is never filled in the parent shell and whose every
22	caller runs it inside `$( )`: 41 calls × 55 manifests. The next third is `yaml_cache_prewarm`
23	(one awk per manifest per key, 55 × 12) and the event bus (a `sed` per key and value, a `jq` per
24	key, a `date` and a `mkdir` per event). None of this is inherent; all of it was invisible because
25	nothing measured it.
26	
27	## Decision
28	
29	### §1 — The number is a contract
30	
31	The engine's external process count on the mocked full run is a tested quantity, held by
32	`tests/e2e/fork-budget-test.sh` as `FORK_BUDGET`. The test runs the parity fixture under bash
33	xtrace (`BASH_ENV` injecting `set -x`, `PS4` stamping `source:line`, `BASH_XTRACEFD=7` — fd 3 is
34	stage-io, 8 is coverage, 9 is flock), classifies each traced command word as external when the
35	test shell resolves it to a file on `PATH` (or it is one of the fixture's mocks), and asserts the
36	total is within budget. Its failure output is the diagnosis: the top call sites and per-file
37	totals, so the next reader starts where the forks are.
38	
39	> **Amended 2026-09-30 (#2236).** The count must not depend on load. The same tree measured 4,528
40	> alone and 4,610 inside a full `npm test`: the worker pool's wait loop
41	> (`core/orch/local_engine.sh`) ran `sleep 0.1` and `date +%s` once per poll, so it counted elapsed
42	> time, not code (18 polls quiet, 44 under load). The clock read is now `$EPOCHSECONDS`, a builtin,
43	> and a wait whose repeat count is elapsed time carries `# fork-budget-exempt: <why>` on its line. The
44	> test lists marked sites apart ("exempt waits") and does not count them. The marker is only for a
45	> poll's wait, never for work: a marked line that execs anything other than the wait hides real forks.
46	
47	### §2 — The budget only ratchets down
48	
49	A PR that removes forks lowers `FORK_BUDGET` to just above its new measurement. A PR that must
50	raise it says why in an amendment to this ADR (the ADR-053 §5 precedent for the serial-pin cap).
51	"It is only a few hundred more" is not a reason; the run-4 postmortem of #1840 is what a few
52	hundred per stage per iteration adds up to.
53	
54	> **Amended 2026-10-01 (#1842): raised to 6,340, with the reason.** The measured fixture
55	> (`tests/golden/parity/run-fixture.sh`) was not running what production runs:
56	> - Its mock repo was never a git repo. `/usr/bin/env git init` resolved to the fixture's own mock `git`, which does nothing.
57	> - Its mock `rev-parse` answered with a made-up path.
58	> - Hydrate, build's diff and persist's snapshot therefore all failed fast and cheaply.
59	> - It ran `review-aggregator` over zero lenses. That "ready" review is what let `pr-open` open a PR (#1753), and #1842 now refuses it.
60	>
61	> The fixture now has a real repo and the production review family, one lens wide. That costs about 1,900 execs that a real run was always paying. Separately, the counter read words inside a quoted assigned value as commands (`v='review lens: security'` counted macOS's `security` binary). That accounted for 132 execs on main's fixture; SPEC-1b holds the fix. Measured: main's fixture 4,367 with the fixed counter, #1842's fixture 6,280 (macOS). The largest new site, persist's two `git` processes per artifact file, is #2249, which ratchets this back down.
62	
63	> **Ratcheted 2026-10-02 (#2249): 6,340 → 5,740.** Persist staged each artifact with two `git` processes; it now stages a whole snapshot with two (`hash-object --stdin-paths`, `update-index --index-info`), and falls back to per-file staging only when a batch fails (#1878). The fixture's local git plumbing now reaches real git, so its snapshots save instead of failing fast. Measured 5,685 on macOS.
64	
65	### §3 — A memo is only as good as its fill in the parent shell
66	
67	`$( … )` and `< <( … )` fork: the child inherits every associative array the parent has filled
68	and can never write back. A memo that is consulted from a subshell but filled only inside one is
69	not a memo — `_inputs_scan_manifests` ran 2,255 awks with its `_IR_SCAN_KEY` guard "in place".
70	The rule: every per-run memo is filled once, in the parent, at a prewarm seam that runs before
71	anything reads it from a subshell (`core/pipeline/runner.sh` warms the yaml cache and discovery
72	at file scope before `core/orch/contract.sh` is sourced — #2105 — and again in `main()`). A memo
73	that cannot be filled in the parent, because the reader is a separately spawned plugin process,
74	may instead be file-backed under `$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/runtime/` with an explicit flush and the
75	shared `ZBUILD_YAML_CACHE=0` kill switch — the `known-event-types.cache` (ADR-001 §Declared
76	events) and `mgraph-memo` (#2129) precedents.
77	
78	### §4 — One pass, not one per key
79	
80	A reader over N manifests forks once — `awk` with an `FNR == 1` reset over the whole file list —
81	never N times and never N × K for K keys. `eb_manifest_events`
82	(`core/event-bus/known-types.sh`) is the existing example. The manifest index (#2152) applies
83	this to the yaml prewarm and `_inputs_scan_manifests`.
84	
85	### §5 — Named, not planned
86	
87	The census also names the event bus's per-event processes, the `$(dirname` / `$(basename` /
88	`$(cat` idioms (363 / 59 / 235 sites in the engine; `${p%/*}`, `${p##*/}`, `$(<f)` are free),
89	`manifest_graph_collect`'s per-hit awk and `cksum`, and `validate_manifest`'s three direct awks
90	per manifest per walk. Each is a later ratchet; this ADR does not schedule them.
91	
92	> **Amended 2026-10-10 (#1806): the event bus's per-event processes are gone.** One
93	> `eb_emit_event` used to start a `jq` per field plus one for the envelope, a `date`, a `mkdir`,
94	> and, with the SQLite mirror on, a `sed` per mirrored field (about 22 for an 11-field event). It
95	> now starts one `jq`, which builds the fields and the envelope together, and the jsonl lock's
96	> `flock`; the mirror adds its `sqlite3` and lock. The clock is `EPOCHREALTIME` read by the shell,
97	> which also gives macOS real milliseconds, and the SQL quoting is a parameter expansion. The
98	> fields reach `jq` as numbered `--arg` pairs, never a positional list, because `jq` reads
99	> options after `--args` and a value such as `-n` must stay a value.
100	> Ratcheted 5,480 → 5,040 (measured 4,991 on macOS).
101	
102	## Consequences
103	
104	- A fork regression fails CI with its call site named, instead of surfacing months later as a
105	  slower daemon.
106	- Test authors get the harness for free: `_fb_traced` + `_fb_count` in the budget test are the
107	  census tool. Run them by hand on any script to see where its forks are.
108	- The number is platform-sensitive at the margin (`gtimeout` vs `timeout`, `stat` flavours);
109	  the budget carries a small headroom and CI's e2e job is Linux-only, so the ratchet is set from
110	  the Linux number.
111	
112	## Implementation Notes (#2151, #2152)
113	
114	- `tests/e2e/fork-budget-test.sh` — `_fb_traced` (the harness), `_fb_count` (the classifier and
115	  tally), `FORK_BUDGET` with its ratchet history in the comment above it.
116	- `core/plugin-registry/manifest-index.sh` (#2152) — the first §4 application: one find + one awk
117	  fill `yaml_cache_prewarm` and `_inputs_scan_manifests`; `core/pipeline/runner.sh` fills the
118	  input-resolve maps at file scope right after sourcing `input-resolve.sh` (§3).
119	- Tests: `manifest-index-test.sh` (equivalence corpus, fork counts, the parent fill),
120	  `yaml-get-cache-test.sh` SPEC-9 (one awk per prewarm).
121	
122	## Verification
123	
124	`bash tests/e2e/fork-budget-test.sh` — SPEC-1 a canary script with one external exec counts
125	exactly 1 (the detector cannot go inert); SPEC-2 the mocked run still exits 0 under tracing;
126	SPEC-3 the trace names ≥ 20 source files and ≥ 1,000 execs (an fd-7-closed child traces to
127	stderr and must not pass as "under budget"); SPEC-4 total ≤ `FORK_BUDGET`. Red step: with the
128	counter stubbed, SPEC-1 fails `expected: 1, got: 0`.
129	
130	## Enforced by
131	
132	- §1 → `tests/e2e/fork-budget-test.sh` SPEC-1 (the canary counts one exec), SPEC-1b (a quoted value is not a command), SPEC-2, SPEC-3, SPEC-4 (the total is within `FORK_BUDGET`)
133	- §1 (amended #2236, exempt waits) → `tests/e2e/fork-budget-test.sh` (marked waits are listed apart and not counted)
134	- §2 → `tests/e2e/fork-budget-test.sh` SPEC-4 (`FORK_BUDGET` carries its ratchet history in the comment above it)
135	- §3, §4 → `tests/unit/manifest-index-test.sh` (fork counts, the parent fill); `tests/unit/yaml-get-cache-test.sh` SPEC-9 (one awk per prewarm)
136	- §5 (amended #1806, the event bus) → `tests/unit/event-bus-emit-cost-test.sh` E1 (one emit starts one `jq` and the lock, nothing per field), E2 (no `sed` for the mirror), E3 (UTC with real milliseconds whatever `ZBUILD_PLATFORM` says), E4 (the envelope is unchanged, and option-like values stay data)
137

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/runner-final-status.sh — pipeline final status helper (#796).
#
# Implements ADR-021 v3 R1: when a cycle exhausts max_iterations with
# on_max=continue, the pipeline final status MUST NOT be terminal failure.
# Downstream stages decide. Only on_max=abort propagates to terminal failure.

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_RUNNER_FINAL_STATUS_LOADED:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    return 0
fi
_ZBUILD_RUNNER_FINAL_STATUS_LOADED=1

_runner_compute_final_status() {
    local unconverged="${1:-0}"
    local on_max="${2:-}"
    local downstream_success="${3:-0}"
    local out_var="$4"

    # Conservative default: empty on_max treated as "abort" (preserves the
    # historical behavior where unconverged → failed regardless).
    [[ -z "$on_max" ]] && on_max="abort"
    # #2241: the template's word is `halt` (cycle-orchestrator accepts
    # continue|halt); `abort` is this file's older word for the same thing.
    [[ "$on_max" == "halt" ]] && on_max="abort"

    # Downstream failure ALWAYS wins.
    if [[ "$downstream_success" != "1" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "failed"
        return 0
    fi

    # Downstream succeeded. Apply on_max semantics:
    if [[ "$unconverged" == "1" && "$on_max" == "abort" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "failed"
        return 0
    fi

    # Downstream succeeded. Distinguish converged vs unconverged:
    # on_max=continue with an unconverged cycle stamps complete_unconverged (#1479).
    if [[ "$unconverged" == "1" && "$on_max" == "continue" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "complete_unconverged"
        return 0
    fi

    printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "complete"
    return 0
}

# _runner_unconverged_msg <cycle_id> <rc> <reason> <on_max> → message on stdout.
# #938: the mid-run warning when a cycle exhausts its budget and the runner
# continues to the next dispatch unit. It MUST match the status that
# _runner_compute_final_status will compute: with on_max=continue the status is
# NOT necessarily 'failed' (it depends on the downstream verdict channel), so
# the old unconditional "pipeline_status will be 'failed'" was stale and
# misleading. #1298: updated to name no stage (ADR-047 stage-agnostic invariant).
_runner_unconverged_msg() {
    local _cyc="${1:-}" _rc="${2:-}" _reason="${3:-}" _on_max="${4:-}"
    if [[ "$_on_max" == "continue" ]]; then
        printf "Cycle %s terminated rc=%s reason=%s — continuing to next dispatch unit (on_max=continue); final pipeline_status depends on the downstream verdict channel" \
            "$_cyc" "$_rc" "$_reason"
    else
        printf "Cycle %s terminated rc=%s reason=%s — continuing to next dispatch unit so the downstream fail-closed gate runs (pipeline_status will be 'failed')" \
            "$_cyc" "$_rc" "$_reason"
    fi
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/run-open-items.sh — what is still open when a run ends, in plain
# words (#2330, ADR-068 §8).
#
# Every place a run reports how it ended — the report of items no stage could
# act on, the live status comment, the issue completion comment, the end-of-run
# banner — names each open item the same way: what is unresolved, and what would
# settle it. The reader may be a person, an agent or a later run, so the words
# say WHAT must be checked, never who must check it, and never the engine's own
# codes (events keep those).
#
# An item comes from the checks' latest results (ADR-068 §8): every check whose
# result did not pass — each of its numbered findings, or its reason when it has
# none. Nothing is kept beside those results.
# A finding may say what would settle it itself, after "What would settle it:".
#
# Source-only; no `set -e` at top level. Needs jq.
[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_RUN_OPEN_ITEMS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_RUN_OPEN_ITEMS_LOADED=1

_OPEN_ITEMS_SETTLE_RE='[[:space:]]*What would settle it:[[:space:]]*'
# The one rule for a check result that passed — every reader of results uses it.
_OPEN_ITEMS_JQ_PASSED='def passed: (.verdict // "" | ascii_downcase)
    | IN("pass", "passed", "approve", "approved", "complete", "success", "skip", "skipped", "");'

# open_items_json <state_dir> — [{ref, opener, text}].
open_items_json() {
    local sd="$1" f
    local -a files=()
    for f in "$sd"/artifacts/*-result.json; do [[ -s "$f" ]] && files+=("$f"); done
    [[ ${#files[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { printf '[]'; return 0; }
    # A result is a check's when it carries a verdict; it is open when that
    # verdict is not a pass. input_filename names the check: <check>-result.json.
    jq -n -c "$_OPEN_ITEMS_JQ_PASSED"'
        [ inputs as $r | (input_filename | split("/") | last | sub("-result\\.json$"; "")) as $c
          | $r | select(type == "object" and (.verdict | type) == "string")
          | select(passed | not)
          | if ((.data.findings // []) | length) > 0 then
                (.data.findings[] | {ref: "\($c) finding \(.n)", opener: $c, text: (.text // "")})
            else
                {ref: $c, opener: $c, text: ("the " + $c + " check did not pass: "
                                              + ((.reason // "") | if . == "" then "it gave no reason" else . end))}
            end ]' "${files[@]}" 2>/dev/null || printf '[]'
}

# open_items_count <state_dir>
open_items_count() {
    jq 'length' <<< "$(open_items_json "$1")" 2>/dev/null || printf '0'
}

# open_items_render <items_json> — the numbered list every report shows. Each
# item: its name and what is unresolved, then what would settle it.
open_items_render() {
    local items="$1"
    jq -r --arg re "$_OPEN_ITEMS_SETTLE_RE" '
        to_entries[] | .key as $i | .value as $it
        | ($it.text // "" | [splits($re)]) as $p
        | ($p[0] | sub("[[:space:]]+$"; "")) as $what
        | (if ($p | length) > 1 and ($p[1:] | join(" ") | length) > 0 then ($p[1:] | join(" "))
           else "the " + $it.opener + " check no longer reports it when it runs again: a change that resolves it, or evidence that it is already resolved"
           end) as $settle
        | "\($i + 1). **\($it.ref)**" + (if $it.ref == $it.opener then "" else " (opened by \($it.opener))" end)
          + ": " + (if $what == "" then "no words were given for it" else $what end)
          + "\n   - What would settle it: " + $settle' <<< "$items" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# open_items_markdown <state_dir> — the list, or nothing when no item is open.
open_items_markdown() {
    local items; items="$(open_items_json "$1")"
    [[ "$items" != "[]" && -n "$items" ]] || return 0
    open_items_render "$items"
}

# _open_items_n <count> <noun> — "1 open item", "2 open items".
_open_items_n() {
    if [[ "$1" == "1" ]]; then printf '1 %s' "$2"; else printf '%s %ss' "$1" "$2"; fi
}

# run_end_words <reason> <open_count> — why the run stopped, in words. <reason>
# is the engine's code (events keep it); the words never repeat it.
run_end_words() {
    local reason="${1:-}" n="${2:-0}" with=""
    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || n=0
    [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] && with=" with $(_open_items_n "$n" "open item")"
    case "$reason" in
        max_iterations|max_iterations_tests_failing)
            printf 'ran out of rounds%s' "$with" ;;
        design_timeout_exhausted)
            printf 'ran out of rounds: the design step did not finish in time%s' "$with" ;;
        blocking_member_failure|member_terminal_failure)
            printf 'stopped: a check that must pass failed%s' "$with" ;;
        blocked|no_committed_changes)
            printf 'stopped: the work could not go further%s' "$with" ;;
        blocked_on_scope)
            printf 'stopped: the change needs files it was not allowed to edit%s' "$with" ;;
        cycle_abort)
            printf 'stopped: a check asked for the run to stop%s' "$with" ;;
        sigterm)
            printf 'stopped: the run was told to stop (TERM signal)%s' "$with" ;;
        sigint)
            printf 'stopped: the run was interrupted (INT signal, Ctrl-C)%s' "$with" ;;
        aborted)
            printf 'stopped: the run was interrupted%s' "$with" ;;
        llm_rate_limited)
            printf 'stopped: the model'"'"'s usage limit was reached%s' "$with" ;;
        llm_unavailable)
            printf 'stopped: the model could not be reached%s' "$with" ;;
        scope_too_large)
            printf 'stopped: the issue is too large to plan in one run — split it%s' "$with" ;;
        stage_failed:*)
            printf 'stopped: a stage reported that it failed (%s)%s' "${reason#stage_failed:}" "$with" ;;
        converged|complete|success)
            printf 'finished%s' "$with" ;;
        *)
            printf 'stopped before finishing%s' "$with" ;;
    esac
}

# run_end_reason <state_dir> — the engine's code for why the run ended: the last
# pipeline.end event's reason, else the state file's. Empty when neither says.
run_end_reason() {
    local sd="$1" r=""
    [[ -s "$sd/events.jsonl" ]] && r="$(jq -r 'select(type == "object" and .type == "pipeline.end") | .data.reason // empty' \
        "$sd/events.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"
    [[ -z "$r" && -s "$sd/pipeline-state.json" ]] && r="$(jq -r '.reason // empty' "$sd/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null)"
    printf '%s' "$r"
}

1	# Claude Code Instructions for zBuild
2	
3	## Source of truth
4	
5	zBuild's architecture and migration plan live in:
6	- [docs/KEEPERS.md](docs/KEEPERS.md) — what we preserve from legacy and why
7	- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — system view, plugin contract, data flow
8	- [docs/adr/](docs/adr/) — formal architecture decisions
9	
10	**If implementation drifts from spec, the spec wins.** PRs cite the relevant ADR or KEEPERS section in the description.
11	
12	### Every ADR statement has a test (#2268)
13	
14	- **A rule that lives only in an ADR's prose is a missing test.** When a run passes something wrong, look first for the ADR statement nothing enforces, and write that test.
15	- **Every live ADR has an `## Enforced by` section** naming, per statement (§), the test or lint that enforces it. A new or changed statement ships with its test in the same PR. `scripts/lib/lint-adr-enforced-by.sh` (in `npm run lint`) fails a live ADR without the section, or one naming a file that does not exist. ADRs written before this rule are listed in `config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt`, which only shrinks.
16	- **Every issue is based on an ADR:** it cites the ADR and § it implements. If no ADR covers the change, the issue first creates one or amends an existing one. ADRs must not contradict each other: a later decision amends the earlier ADR in the same PR.
17	
18	## Behavioral rules
19	
20	- Do what has been asked; nothing more, nothing less.
21	- ALWAYS read a file before editing it.
22	- NEVER create files unless necessary for the task.
23	- NEVER proactively create documentation files (`*.md`) or READMEs unless explicitly requested.
24	- NEVER save working files, tests, or scratch markdown to the root folder.
25	- NEVER commit secrets, credentials, or `.env` files.
26	- Keep files under 500 lines unless there is a strong reason.
27	
28	## File organization
29	
30	- `/core` — engine: safety primitives, plugin registry, event bus, dispatch
31	- `/plugins` — plugin implementations, one directory per plugin
32	- `/config` — config files (models.json, event-schema.json)
33	- `/scripts` — CLI entry + shared libs
34	- `/tests` — all tests; `/tests/golden` for snapshot diffs
35	- `/docs` — KEEPERS, ARCHITECTURE, ADRs, plans
36	- `/legacy-DoNotUse` — frozen upstream import; FROZEN, do not run, do not read as zBuild code
37	- `/.github` — workflows, issue templates, `keepers-manifest.yaml`
38	
39	## Working with `legacy-DoNotUse/`
40	
41	- `legacy-DoNotUse/` is a frozen reference copy of shipwright, kept only so KEEPERS citations resolve. It is not zBuild code: nothing in `core/`, `plugins/`, `scripts/` or `tests/` reads it, and issue worktrees leave it out entirely (ADR-059 §2). **DO NOT EDIT files in `legacy-DoNotUse/`** except `legacy-DoNotUse/.shipwright-disabled` (the sentinel) and `legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/sw` (one-line patch documented in ADR-002).
42	- The only legitimate way to remove `legacy-DoNotUse/` content is pruning: when a keeper's replacement lands, `git rm` its legacy source in the same PR. Nothing else is written — there are no tombstones. Anything a maintainer needs to know about the replacement goes where it belongs (the plugin's README, the ADR, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`), as a statement about our code (ADR-002, amended 2026-10-09).
43	- Never run scripts under `legacy-DoNotUse/` directly; the sentinel will refuse to run anyway, but assume daemon-level state pollution risk if you bypass it.
44	
45	## Migration discipline
46	
47	- Each keeper from KEEPERS.md gets one issue (template in `.github/issues/keepers-manifest.yaml`).
48	- Issue PRs include the 5-test trial checklist in the description, marked complete before merge.
49	- After a keeper merges, its legacy source is removed (`git rm`) in the same PR; nothing else is written.
50	- Phase milestones gate progression: Phase 1 issues are blocked until Phase 0 ships.
51	- **Test scope discovery**: before listing test files in scope for any issue that changes pipeline stage counts, template shape, or dispatch units, run `grep -rl <hardcoded-value> tests/` to find every test that pins that value. All matches must be in the issue's scope — a missed file causes build-loop failures that can't be fixed within the plan's scope enforcement.
52	
53	## Build & Test
54	
55	```bash
56	# Install
57	./install.sh
58	
59	# Test
60	npm test           # full bash test suite
61	npm run test:unit  # unit tests only
62	npm run lint       # shellcheck + lint
63	```
64	
65	- **Write the test first.** Before editing any file under `core/`, `plugins/`, or `scripts/`,
66	  write (or amend) the test that expresses the required behavior, run it, and confirm it FAILS —
67	  and fails for the reason you intend, not on a typo or a missing fixture. Only then write the
68	  implementation. Then re-run and watch it go green.
69	- **A test written after the implementation asserts what the code does, not what was required.**
70	  This is not a style preference — it is the defect class that shipped #1919: its test asserted
71	  the grant was "exactly the repo root + stage scratch", a faithful description of the code, which
72	  therefore stayed green while every design stage died on a refused write (#1961). Order the work
73	  so the test cannot be shaped by the implementation.
74	- **Reverting the implementation afterwards to check the test goes red is NOT test-first.** It
75	  produces the same two files and a weaker test, because the assertion was still authored while
76	  looking at the code. Use it to verify an inherited test, never as a substitute for the ordering.
77	- **State the red step in the PR body**: the assertion, and how it failed before the fix.
78	- **Data another part of the engine writes is checked against its writer** (#1799). When a change reads
79	  something another part of the code writes — pipeline-state.json, another stage's result, an event — open
80	  the writer and use the names it really writes, when it writes them. A test makes such data with the
81	  writer's own code (e.g. `zb_engine_loop_state` for loop state; `lint-test-engine-state.sh` refuses a
82	  hand-written `cycle_iterations`), never by hand: hand-made data holds whatever its author assumed. A
83	  review of such a change checks this too.
84	- ALWAYS run tests after making code changes.
85	- CI enforces a **29% statement coverage floor** on `core/` + `scripts/lib/` (issue #372, raised in Wave 4). Target is 70% — will be raised incrementally as test depth improves. If Coverage CI fails, run `bash scripts/check-coverage.sh` locally to see per-file coverage. The denominator counts every in-scope `.sh` file on disk, including ones no test ever sources (#1761) — a new untested file lowers the number rather than being invisible to it.
86	- ALWAYS verify the relevant test passes before opening a PR.
87	
88	## Security rules
89	
90	- NEVER hardcode API keys, secrets, or credentials in source files.
91	- NEVER commit `.env` files.
92	- Validate user input at system boundaries (the CLI, GitHub label parsers, plugin manifests).
93	- Sanitize file paths to prevent directory traversal.
94	- All LLM-bound text passes through `core/redaction/apply_scope_redaction` — no exceptions. A plugin that invokes a model directly is a bug.
95	
96	## Code style
97	
98	- **Function headers**: one-line comment above a function only when the WHY is non-obvious (hidden constraint, workaround, invariant). Never multi-line docstrings. Apply this on touch — no mass backfill.
99	- **Shellcheck**: `.shellcheckrc` at repo root sets `shell=bash` and disables SC1090/SC1091 (dynamic source paths). Per-file `# shellcheck disable=SCXXXX` is still fine for local suppressions.
100	- **Editor conventions**: `.editorconfig` at repo root: 4-space indent for `.sh`, 2-space for YAML/JSON, LF line endings, final newline, no trailing whitespace.
101	- **No SIGPIPE-prone pipes**: never `printf`/`echo "$var" | grep -q`, and no bare `| head`, in `scripts/`, `core/`, or `plugins/`. The reader exits early, the writer takes SIGPIPE, and under `set -euo pipefail` the surrounding function dies for a reason nothing logs. Use a here-string (`grep -q ... <<< "$var"`), or capture in full and trim in bash. `tests/unit/sigpipe-antipattern-guard-test.sh` enforces this; a genuinely safe pipe is annotated `# sigpipe-ok: <reason>`.
102	
103	## Models as data, not strings
104	
105	- Code never references `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`, etc. by name.
106	- All model selection goes through `core/router` reading `config/models.json`.
107	- Tier ordinals (T0–T4) are stable; model names change. (See ADR-003.)

=== runner-final-status.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/runner-final-status.sh — pipeline final status helper (#796).
#
# Implements ADR-021 v3 R1: when a cycle exhausts max_iterations with
# on_max=continue, the pipeline final status MUST NOT be terminal failure.
# Downstream stages decide. Only on_max=abort propagates to terminal failure.

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_RUNNER_FINAL_STATUS_LOADED:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    return 0
fi
_ZBUILD_RUNNER_FINAL_STATUS_LOADED=1

_runner_compute_final_status() {
    local unconverged="${1:-0}"
    local on_max="${2:-}"
    local downstream_success="${3:-0}"
    local out_var="$4"

    # Conservative default: empty on_max treated as "abort" (preserves the
    # historical behavior where unconverged → failed regardless).
    [[ -z "$on_max" ]] && on_max="abort"
    # #2241: the template's word is `halt` (cycle-orchestrator accepts
    # continue|halt); `abort` is this file's older word for the same thing.
    [[ "$on_max" == "halt" ]] && on_max="abort"

    # Downstream failure ALWAYS wins.
    if [[ "$downstream_success" != "1" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "failed"
        return 0
    fi

    # Downstream succeeded. Apply on_max semantics:
    if [[ "$unconverged" == "1" && "$on_max" == "abort" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "failed"
        return 0
    fi

    # Downstream succeeded. Distinguish converged vs unconverged:
    # on_max=continue with an unconverged cycle stamps complete_unconverged (#1479).
    if [[ "$unconverged" == "1" && "$on_max" == "continue" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "complete_unconverged"
        return 0
    fi

    printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "complete"
    return 0
}

# _runner_unconverged_msg <cycle_id> <rc> <reason> <on_max> → message on stdout.
# #938: the mid-run warning when a cycle exhausts its budget and the runner
# continues to the next dispatch unit. It MUST match the status that
# _runner_compute_final_status will compute: with on_max=continue the status is
# NOT necessarily 'failed' (it depends on the downstream verdict channel), so
# the old unconditional "pipeline_status will be 'failed'" was stale and
# misleading. #1298: updated to name no stage (ADR-047 stage-agnostic invariant).
_runner_unconverged_msg() {
    local _cyc="${1:-}" _rc="${2:-}" _reason="${3:-}" _on_max="${4:-}"
    if [[ "$_on_max" == "continue" ]]; then
        printf "Cycle %s terminated rc=%s reason=%s — continuing to next dispatch unit (on_max=continue); final pipeline_status depends on the downstream verdict channel" \
            "$_cyc" "$_rc" "$_reason"
    else
        printf "Cycle %s terminated rc=%s reason=%s — continuing to next dispatch unit so the downstream fail-closed gate runs (pipeline_status will be 'failed')" \
            "$_cyc" "$_rc" "$_reason"
    fi
}

=== runner-final-status.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/runner-final-status.sh — pipeline final status helper (#796).
#
# Implements ADR-021 v3 R1: when a cycle exhausts max_iterations with
# on_max=continue, the pipeline final status MUST NOT be terminal failure.
# Downstream stages decide. Only on_max=abort propagates to terminal failure.

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_RUNNER_FINAL_STATUS_LOADED:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    return 0
fi
_ZBUILD_RUNNER_FINAL_STATUS_LOADED=1

_runner_compute_final_status() {
    local unconverged="${1:-0}"
    local on_max="${2:-}"
    local downstream_success="${3:-0}"
    local out_var="$4"

    # Conservative default: empty on_max treated as "abort" (preserves the
    # historical behavior where unconverged → failed regardless).
    [[ -z "$on_max" ]] && on_max="abort"
    # #2241: the template's word is `halt` (cycle-orchestrator accepts
    # continue|halt); `abort` is this file's older word for the same thing.
    [[ "$on_max" == "halt" ]] && on_max="abort"

    # Downstream failure ALWAYS wins.
    if [[ "$downstream_success" != "1" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "failed"
        return 0
    fi

    # Downstream succeeded. Apply on_max semantics:
    if [[ "$unconverged" == "1" && "$on_max" == "abort" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "failed"
        return 0
    fi

    # Downstream succeeded. Distinguish converged vs unconverged:
    # on_max=continue with an unconverged cycle stamps complete_unconverged (#1479).
    if [[ "$unconverged" == "1" && "$on_max" == "continue" ]]; then
        printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "complete_unconverged"
        return 0
    fi

    printf -v "$out_var" '%s' "complete"
    return 0
}

# _runner_unconverged_msg <cycle_id> <rc> <reason> <on_max> → message on stdout.
# #938: the mid-run warning when a cycle exhausts its budget and the runner
# continues to the next dispatch unit. It MUST match the status that
# _runner_compute_final_status will compute: with on_max=continue the status is
# NOT necessarily 'failed' (it depends on the downstream verdict channel), so
# the old unconditional "pipeline_status will be 'failed'" was stale and
# misleading. #1298: updated to name no stage (ADR-047 stage-agnostic invariant).
_runner_unconverged_msg() {
    local _cyc="${1:-}" _rc="${2:-}" _reason="${3:-}" _on_max="${4:-}"
    if [[ "$_on_max" == "continue" ]]; then
        printf "Cycle %s terminated rc=%s reason=%s — continuing to next dispatch unit (on_max=continue); final pipeline_status depends on the downstream verdict channel" \
            "$_cyc" "$_rc" "$_reason"
    else
        printf "Cycle %s terminated rc=%s reason=%s — continuing to next dispatch unit so the downstream fail-closed gate runs (pipeline_status will be 'failed')" \
            "$_cyc" "$_rc" "$_reason"
    fi
}

For SPEC-3, the process-group behavior gets tested by spawning a TERM-ignoring child process within the group and confirming it's gone after TERM followed by a 10s wait before KILL.

SPEC-6 (always-run stages after timeout) is checked in run-timed-out-test.sh, and SPEC-7 (fresh limit on resume) is covered in resume-after-run-timeout-test.sh, confirming a resumed run doesn't immediately re-time-out.

I also want to distinguish SPEC-3 from SPEC-1: R-3 is about the run-level watchdog correctly invoking the existing zbuild_pg_kill to terminate the run's process group, not about the kill mechanism itself, which already has its own coverage.

The runner's EXIT trap kills the watchdog PID to disarm it, always-run stages like release/persist still fire through the existing dispatch mechanism, resume behavior re-arms the watchdog fresh each time with no persisted state, and there's no platform-specific branching needed. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh — ADR-025 abort-propagation contract (Wave 15-B, #684)
#
# An abort is RECORDED once, as a word, and every dispatcher asks for it at the
# same two points in its loop (#1850, ADR-054 §4 — no rc carries the reason):
#
#   loop {
#       _zbuild_check_abort || return 1             # pre-flight
#       dispatch_child
#       _zbuild_propagate_abort $? || return 1      # post-flight
#   }
#
# Words: sigint | sigterm | cycle_abort | llm_unavailable | llm_rate_limited |
# scope_too_large. The first recorded abort wins.
#
# Two channels hold the word: `_ZB_ABORT_REASON` in this process, and the
# sentinel file ${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal, which crosses subshells and
# `_zbuild_make_fresh_shell` env scrubs (ADR-024) where a variable does not.
# An EMPTY sentinel reads as `sigint` — what arming wrote before it took a word.
#
# Sourced library: no `set -euo pipefail` (would mutate caller options).

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ABORT_PROP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ABORT_PROP_LOADED=1

# Empty when ZBUILD_STATE_DIR is unset: the helpers then keep the word in-process
# only, rather than fabricate a path under cwd.
_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path() {
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}" ]]; then
        printf '%s/.abort.signal' "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
    fi
}

_zbuild_abort_reason() {
    if [[ -n "${_ZB_ABORT_REASON:-}" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_ZB_ABORT_REASON"
        return 0
    fi
    local _sentinel _word=""
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -n "$_sentinel" && -e "$_sentinel" ]] || return 0
    IFS= read -r _word 2>/dev/null < "$_sentinel" || true
    printf '%s' "${_word:-sigint}"
}

# Best-effort: a failed sentinel write must not fail a signal trap — the
# in-process word still holds the abort.
_zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel() {
    local _word="${1:-sigint}" _sentinel _dir _prior
    _prior="$(_zbuild_abort_reason)"
    if [[ -n "$_prior" ]]; then
        _ZB_ABORT_REASON="$_prior"
        return 0
    fi
    _ZB_ABORT_REASON="$_word"
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -z "$_sentinel" ]] && return 0
    _dir="$(dirname "$_sentinel")"
    [[ -d "$_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    printf '%s\n' "$_word" > "$_sentinel" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# Called by the runner's EXIT trap and by --resume, so a later run in the same
# state dir does not see a stale abort.
_zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel() {
    local _sentinel
    unset _ZB_ABORT_REASON
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -z "$_sentinel" ]] && return 0
    [[ -e "$_sentinel" ]] && rm -f "$_sentinel" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# Returns 1 so a caller can write `_zbuild_abort <word>; return` or `|| return 1`.
_zbuild_abort() {
    _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel "${1:-sigint}"
    return 1
}

_zbuild_check_abort() {
    [[ -n "$(_zbuild_abort_reason)" ]] && return 1
    return 0
}

# 1 only when the child failed AND an abort is recorded: an ordinary failure is
# the caller's to handle, and a child that succeeded is not an abort.
_zbuild_propagate_abort() {
    [[ "${1:-0}" == "0" ]] && return 0
    _zbuild_check_abort
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh — ADR-025 abort-propagation contract (Wave 15-B, #684)
#
# An abort is RECORDED once, as a word, and every dispatcher asks for it at the
# same two points in its loop (#1850, ADR-054 §4 — no rc carries the reason):
#
#   loop {
#       _zbuild_check_abort || return 1             # pre-flight
#       dispatch_child
#       _zbuild_propagate_abort $? || return 1      # post-flight
#   }
#
# Words: sigint | sigterm | cycle_abort | llm_unavailable | llm_rate_limited |
# scope_too_large. The first recorded abort wins.
#
# Two channels hold the word: `_ZB_ABORT_REASON` in this process, and the
# sentinel file ${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal, which crosses subshells and
# `_zbuild_make_fresh_shell` env scrubs (ADR-024) where a variable does not.
# An EMPTY sentinel reads as `sigint` — what arming wrote before it took a word.
#
# Sourced library: no `set -euo pipefail` (would mutate caller options).

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ABORT_PROP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ABORT_PROP_LOADED=1

# Empty when ZBUILD_STATE_DIR is unset: the helpers then keep the word in-process
# only, rather than fabricate a path under cwd.
_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path() {
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}" ]]; then
        printf '%s/.abort.signal' "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
    fi
}

_zbuild_abort_reason() {
    if [[ -n "${_ZB_ABORT_REASON:-}" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_ZB_ABORT_REASON"
        return 0
    fi
    local _sentinel _word=""
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -n "$_sentinel" && -e "$_sentinel" ]] || return 0
    IFS= read -r _word 2>/dev/null < "$_sentinel" || true
    printf '%s' "${_word:-sigint}"
}

# Best-effort: a failed sentinel write must not fail a signal trap — the
# in-process word still holds the abort.
_zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel() {
    local _word="${1:-sigint}" _sentinel _dir _prior
    _prior="$(_zbuild_abort_reason)"
    if [[ -n "$_prior" ]]; then
        _ZB_ABORT_REASON="$_prior"
        return 0
    fi
    _ZB_ABORT_REASON="$_word"
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -z "$_sentinel" ]] && return 0
    _dir="$(dirname "$_sentinel")"
    [[ -d "$_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    printf '%s\n' "$_word" > "$_sentinel" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# Called by the runner's EXIT trap and by --resume, so a later run in the same
# state dir does not see a stale abort.
_zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel() {
    local _sentinel
    unset _ZB_ABORT_REASON
    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
    [[ -z "$_sentinel" ]] && return 0
    [[ -e "$_sentinel" ]] && rm -f "$_sentinel" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# Returns 1 so a caller can write `_zbuild_abort <word>; return` or `|| return 1`.
_zbuild_abort() {
    _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel "${1:-sigint}"
    return 1
}

_zbuild_check_abort() {
    [[ -n "$(_zbuild_abort_reason)" ]] && return 1
    return 0
}

# 1 only when the child failed AND an abort is recorded: an ordinary failure is
# the caller's to handle, and a child that succeeded is not an abort.
_zbuild_propagate_abort() {
    [[ "${1:-0}" == "0" ]] && return 0
    _zbuild_check_abort
}

2:# Tests: core/pipeline/runner.sh — _render_pipeline_end terminal banner (#525)
4:# Covers the operator-visible banner emitted at every pipeline.end / EXIT-trap
6:#   - per-status glyph + color resolution (delegates to verdict.sh helpers)
7:#   - NO_COLOR strips ANSI but preserves glyph + timestamp + status text
8:#   - unknown status falls back to '?' glyph defensively
12:# ADR-015 §v5 amendment / ADR-006 pipeline status enum.
17:GOLDEN_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/tests/golden/pipeline-end"
22:print_test_header "core/pipeline/runner — pipeline.end terminal banner (#525)"
23:setup_test_env "runner-pipeline-end"
30:    local mode="$1" status="$2" stage="${3:-}" rc="${4:-}" run_id="${5:-r1}" issue="${6:-83}"
32:    if [[ "$mode" == "layout" ]]; then
50:        _render_pipeline_end '$status' '$stage' '$rc'
54:# ─── T1: glyph + status text per status class (layout mode) ──────────────────
55:out="$(emit_banner layout complete)"
56:assert_contains "T1a complete banner uses ✓ glyph"        "$out" "✓"
57:assert_contains "T1a complete banner uses 'complete' word" "$out" "Pipeline complete:"
58:assert_contains "T1a complete banner carries status=complete" "$out" "status=complete"
60:out="$(emit_banner layout failed build 1)"
61:assert_contains "T1b failed banner uses ✗ glyph"  "$out" "✗"
62:assert_contains "T1b failed banner reports stage" "$out" "stage=build"
63:assert_contains "T1b failed banner reports rc"    "$out" "rc=1"
65:out="$(emit_banner layout interrupted)"
66:assert_contains "T1c interrupted banner uses ✗ glyph"   "$out" "✗"
67:assert_contains "T1c interrupted banner word"           "$out" "Pipeline interrupted:"
69:out="$(emit_banner layout aborted)"
70:assert_contains "T1d aborted banner uses ✗ glyph"  "$out" "✗"
71:assert_contains "T1d aborted banner word"          "$out" "Pipeline aborted:"
73:out="$(emit_banner layout preflight_failed)"
74:assert_contains "T1e preflight_failed banner uses ⚠ glyph"   "$out" "⚠"
75:assert_contains "T1e preflight_failed banner word tracks status" "$out" "Pipeline preflight_failed:"
77:# ─── T2: colored mode carries ANSI escapes per status class ──────────────────
78:out_c="$(emit_banner colored complete)"
81:# Just check for a SGR escape + verdict_color is non-empty in colored mode.
82:assert_contains "T2a colored complete carries an ANSI escape" "$out_c" $'\033['
83:out_c="$(emit_banner colored failed build 1)"
84:assert_contains "T2b colored failed carries an ANSI escape"   "$out_c" $'\033['
85:out_c="$(emit_banner colored preflight_failed)"
86:assert_contains "T2c colored preflight_failed carries an ANSI escape" "$out_c" $'\033['
89:out_l="$(emit_banner layout complete)"
92:    assert_fail "T3 NO_COLOR strips ANSI" "ESC byte found in layout-mode banner"
=== ADR-025 Enforced-by section ===
11:Three consecutive discoveries of the same abort-propagation bug class —
61:`scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh`. Signature:
90:`scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh`. Signature:
251:  `_zbuild_check_abort` in `scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh`, convert
326:  `scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh`. The first returns its argument rc when the argument is an abort rc
363:ADR-054 §4 makes exit codes binary everywhere, the engine's own paths included. This ADR's two layers carried the abort *as* an rc (130, then 143, and later 6, 9 and 10 joined), and every reader mapped those numbers its own way — `cycle_orchestrator_run` collapsed a nested `cycle_abort` into `config_invalid` (#1860). The layers stay; what they carry changes.
372:## Enforced by
374:- Decision, both layers (#1850: the abort is recorded once as a word, in-process and in the sentinel; the first wins; every helper returns 0 or 1; no state dir → in-process only) → `tests/unit/abort-propagation-test.sh` A1–A9
406:- `scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh` — forthcoming home of
=== ADR-054 §9 ===
7:**Amended:** 2026-09-16 (#2111) — §6: a rate limit observed by the router resolves to `unavailable`, not `throttled`. The engine now enforces `halt_unavailable` on the cycle dispatch path (it was announced only): the run ends `aborted` with `reason=llm_rate_limited` and the reset text under `.rate_limit.message`, state persisted for ADR-050 resume. `throttled` stays in the closed set with no rate-limit emitter. Waiting and retrying re-entered the same limit for five iterations on #1840/#1841, re-verifying an unchanged tree each time.
8:**Amended:** 2026-08-23 (#141) — §7: the three-actor table is run-keyed in every row; the **issue** is a second scope, and `release` gains the `always-run` attribute plus a `persist` sibling (ADR-059).
9:**Amended:** 2026-08-23 (#1920) — §7: the `release` "deletes nothing" promise scoped to the run's own lifecycle; operator-invoked reclamation (`zbuild cleanup --state-dirs`) named as a third actor with its own clock and guards.
67:- `scope` — `release` or `purge` (§7).
108:- `ZBUILD_UNIT` is `<stage>.<element>` for a map member (the declared element, or the platform for a map over platforms) and the stage name otherwise. It lives for one dispatch, like the rest of this table. A stage dispatched from inside a member is named by its own stage. Enforced by `tests/unit/unit-name-test.sh` U1–U3.
109:- An engine event emitted inside a member carries `unit` in its envelope; an event outside a map carries no `unit` key, so every other envelope is unchanged. Enforced by U4.
110:- Per-member records are named by the unit; the router's error record is the first (`<unit>-sync-error`). Enforced by U5. The router's throttle and turn-budget markers stay keyed by stage, because the runner reads them at the group level, outside the members.
111:- A map that runs more than one role runs every role on every element, so the role is part of the name: `<stage>.<role>.<element>`. Enforced by U7.
112:- **Two units with one name never start together.** A map whose members would share a name is refused before any member starts (rc 1 — failed, per §4; the `strategy.unit_name_conflict` event names the duplicate). Enforced by U6.
226:| `exhausted` | More budget, or the work must shrink. **(retired 2026-09-25 by §6a / #2187 — now `out_of_turns` or `timed_out`, response: retry)** |
248:| `timed_out` | it ran out of time | retry |
261:- **Migrated (#2187 PR 2):** every v2 stage now sends the cause word — a model's unusable output → `unusable`; a scope violation or a false completion → `complete` with that verdict; a setup failure (no model tier, the router's own rc=2 checks) → `misconfigured`; a missing engine-promised input → `broken`. Model-call failures are named in ONE place, `router_reason_disposition` (`scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh`), which the router feeds a turn-budget hit as `router_out_of_turns`. `exhausted` is retired and `broken` halts. "Did not finish" is the predicate `disposition_unfinished` (timed_out, out_of_turns, interrupted), not one word. `scripts/lib/lint-disposition-words.sh` (npm run lint + CI Lint) rejects a literal off-set word.
282:| `release` | Automatic, at end of work | Frees live resources: kills spawned process groups, closes handles, releases locks | **Deletes nothing** |
285:No → `release`. Yes → `purge`. The rule exists because the inverse destroys evidence: `plugins/tool/test/plugin.sh` `rm -rf`s its staging dir on return and kills nothing, which is exactly backwards — orphaned suites keep running against a deleted tree (#1748).
291:`release` deletes nothing, so a run that fails still owns its complete evidence at the moment it ends, and neither a normal exit nor a trap can take that away. That is the promise, and it is unchanged.
293:It was read more broadly than it says. `purge` was the only named deleter of a run's persisted state, and `purge` is reachable only through `zbuild clean --purge`, so a job folder was in practice permanent — including for the ~190 runs that had already accumulated when #1920 measured it. ADR-058 recorded that as an accepted cost, and named #1920 as the issue that would fix it.
297:| | `release` | `purge` | `zbuild cleanup --state-dirs` |
309:Every actor above is scoped to a **run**: `release` frees the run's live resources, `purge` deletes
310:the run's persisted state, and `zbuild cleanup --state-dirs` reclaims a run's job folder. That was
316:- **`release` gains an always-run declaration and a sibling.** §7's release becomes a template stage
317:  carrying the `always-run` attribute, and ADR-059 §3 adds `persist` beside it — always-run, later,
318:  with a longer timeout, because it does network I/O and release must stay fast enough that Ctrl-C
327:**An always-run stage's time bound stops the stage, not just the wait — amended 2026-10-04 (#2287).**
328:Each always-run stage runs under a bound: its own `router.timeout_s` from the template, or
334:TERM is not spared when the bound's watchdog is cancelled (#2333). No process from an always-run
335:stage outlives the run. Enforced by `tests/integration/runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` SPEC-6
401:- `core/router/route.sh` — `_route_resolve_knob` and the per-knob resolvers (§9).
431:A retry (§6a) dispatches the stage again, and each dispatch writes its result to the same path. The result must still describe **everything the stage did in that cycle round**, not only its last pass. On #2032 run 37289606005, round 2's build committed one file on its first pass, ended on three router timeouts (`timed_out`), was re-dispatched, and changed nothing on the second pass; the result then read "changed 0 file(s) over 1 iteration(s)".
